title: Gideon and the Clock
premise: In 1893, Casper Whitlock, a young woman passing as a male apprentice clockmaker, is sent to repair the failing master clock of a remote mountain observatory just as the seasonal bridge closes, stranding her there for months. She finds the observatory staff fractured: an aging astronomer clinging to his fading reputation, his estranged daughter keeping the household alive, and a stargazing handyman who sees through her disguise and says nothing. As she restores the clock, Casper uncovers that the astronomer has been falsifying observations to secure funding — and that exposing him would destroy the found family she's finally begun to belong to. In the end, she repairs both the clock and the truth, convincing him to publish honest corrections before the bridge reopens, choosing to stay through another winter not by accident but by choice.
about_author: I. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent years restoring Victorian scientific instruments. Their fiction explores the quiet dramas of people who keep time, light, and machines running for others.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Summoned to the observatory under her late master's name, she arrives disguised as a man, determined to finish the repair quickly and vanish back into anonymity. The bridge closes behind her sooner than expected. Emotional beat: unease — her plan for invisibility collapses in a single afternoon.

chapters.title: What the Pendulum Keeps
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, with interludes from Marta, the astronomer's daughter. Working inside the clock tower, Casper bonds with Marta over shared labor and secrets, while noticing discrepancies in the observation ledgers. The handyman, Tobias, quietly acknowledges her disguise without betrayal. Emotional beat: cautious warmth — belonging begins to feel possible.

chapters.title: The Hour That Lies
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She confirms the astronomer, Dr. Halloran, has falsified star charts to secure funding, and confronts him privately; he threatens to expose her identity if she speaks. A storm damages the observatory roof, and the household must work together through the night. Emotional beat: dread and loyalty at war — the climax of competing truths.

chapters.title: Setting the Hands Right
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. During the repair's final days, she persuades Halloran to publish corrections himself, offering him the dignity of confession over ruin; he relents, seeing his own reflection in her hidden life. The master clock strikes true for the first time in years. When the bridge reopens, Casper chooses to stay. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging chosen, not stumbled into.
